answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network uses a dynamic stake-burning registry. Each node must commit tokens into a quadratic burn pool parameterized like fractured shale strata, where registering N identities requires burning O(N^2) tokens. A verifiable beacon emits periodic entropy pulses, forcing each identity to generate a cryptographic cipher proof to maintain validity. This mechanism imposes superlinear cost scaling, making coordinated Sybil swarms exponentially unprofitable.
